grounding_items.sentence: FlashAttention‑2 revises the original FlashAttention pipeline by reshaping how work is divided among GPU resources.
grounding_items.label: UNSUPPORTED

grounding_items.sentence: First, the algorithm is altered to cut the number of non‑matrix‑multiply floating‑point operations, which were a dominant source of overhead in the earlier design.
grounding_items.label: SUPPORTED

grounding_items.sentence: Second, attention is parallelized across multiple thread blocks even when a single head is processed, raising occupancy and allowing more of the GPU’s compute units to stay busy.
grounding_items.label: SUPPORTED

grounding_items.sentence: Third, within each thread block the workload is spread among warps, which reduces the amount of data that must pass through shared memory and therefore lowers intra‑block communication costs.
grounding_items.label: SUPPORTED

grounding_items.sentence: These three engineering changes directly address the sub‑optimal work partitioning that limited the original FlashAttention to only 25‑40 % of the theoretical FLOPs / s on A100 GPUs and prevented it from matching the efficiency of dense GEMM kernels.
grounding_items.label: SUPPORTED

grounding_items.sentence: The original method relied on tiling and an online soft‑max to cut memory traffic, delivering 2‑4× wall‑clock speedups over baseline attention implementations but still falling short of GEMM performance.
grounding_items.label: SUPPORTED

grounding_items.sentence: By applying the new partitioning strategy, FlashAttention‑2 doubles the effective throughput of the baseline FlashAttention implementation, achieving roughly a 2× speedup and reaching 50‑73 % of the theoretical maximum FLOPs / s on A100 hardware, which is close to the efficiency of optimized matrix‑multiply operations.
grounding_items.label: SUPPORTED

grounding_items.sentence: In end‑to‑end GPT‑style training this translates to up to 225 TFLOPs / s per A100 GPU, corresponding to a model‑level FLOPs utilization of about 72 %.
grounding_items.label: SUPPORTED
